task: explore: open-tennis-robots hopper agitator (flagship buildable item)
errors: A design check (arm band round a floor ball's centre) could never fire because the arm is centred there by construction; found when writing its failing-value test, and removed.
First motor-mount concept put the hub boss through the motor's face-screw circle (PCD 17 inside a 16 mm boss hole); redesigned so the hub grips only the shaft's top end above the tub floor.

doc_friction.issue: A feeder package build takes about 10 minutes on 4 CPUs and the README does not say so; a run that rebuilds it twice (as this one did, for a README.txt template line) should start it in the background early.
FEEDER_README's 'NOT IN THIS PACKAGE YET' line is hand-maintained text inside the generated package, so changing it forces a second 10-minute rebuild; it could be derived from the parts list.

notes: Explore idea: take the open-tennis-robots flagship's unclaimed buildable item, the hopper agitator. Geometry first (bridging balls over a 75 mm outlet are floor balls with centres at 33.5 mm), so two printed arms sweep at that height on a shaft normal to the tub floor from a 25 mm gearmotor under the shelf, placed clear of the sleeve socket flange and take-up spring. Eleven design checks (each with a failing-value test), firmware AgitatorRun on GPIO 17 while balls are wanted plus 3 s, tub envelope made an open box. Feeder package rebuilt: design rules pass, no collisions in the elevation, azimuth, feed-stroke and cable sweeps. Local checks: open-tennis-robots python suite (76 tests) and node tests (21) pass; CAD unittest run against the rebuilt package.
